The Countess

Mistress of Runes

Forgotten Tower L5 · Act 1 · ONLY rune-dedicated drop table

tier
S+
▾
Why farm: Only monster with a dedicated rune table. Best Ist source (1:1,110 Hell). ~30-50 runs/hour with teleport. Drop ceiling: Lo rune (Hell), Ist (Hell). NO Mal+ from Countess.
📋 Action plan: Black Marsh waypoint → Tower (look for stairs into Tower Cellar) → take stairs down to Level 5 → kill Countess in the chamber → exit + reset. Each Countess kill = 3 simultaneous rune rolls.
📊 Rune drop notes: Rune drop rates ARE NOT affected by MF. They're affected only by difficulty + monster level + Players count. Higher Players setting = more chances but each individual drop has lower probability. P1 = best for solo runes on Countess (max kill speed, simpler math).

Herald of Terror Sunder Source

Hell-TZ superunique · apex of the 5-tier Herald ladder · the grail-of-grails Sunder source.
spawns: Hell Terror Zones only · roams the active TZ feeds → Latent Sunder Charms · Worldstone Shards
sunder source
★
🎯 What it is
A roaming mini-boss that spawns inside Hell Terror Zones and hunts you across the map. Put it down to loot Latent Sunder Charms — the only way to break monster immunities in RotW — and, because Heralds are superunique-tier, the occasional Worldstone Shard (the charm-upgrade fragment).
📍 Where it spawns
categoryHell-TZ superunique
spawn rate~2% ire per elite kill → ~1% per fresh-tile monster
feeds intoLatent Sunder → Renewed Sunder
MF affects?no — speed > MF (post-3.2)
spawns inHell Terror Zones only — never Normal/Nightmare, never outside a TZ; roams the active TZ and hunts you across the map
noteSuperunique-tier loot: Latent Sunder Charms (the only immunity-break in RotW) plus the occasional Worldstone Shard (the charm-upgrade fragment). Post-3.2 every tier can drop a Latent.
👹 The 5 Herald tiers — open each ID card
Each kill bumps the next Herald one tier higher — climb Fright → Dread → Fear → Horror → Terror. Click any tier for its full ID card; each is also globally searchable by its own name.
Herald of Fright
tier 1 · base event stats · standard elite loot
Herald of Dread
tier 2 · ↑ HP & damage · standard elite loot
Herald of Fear
tier 3 · aggressive combat auras · low Sunder chance
Herald of Horror
tier 4 · extreme damage output · +1 extra item · Sunder threshold opens
Herald of Terror
tier 5 · apex · maximum scaling · +2 extra items · optimal Latent Sunder rate
⚠ Tiers reset to Fright if you exit to the main menu — stay in one game session to keep climbing. Once you hit Terror, every Herald the rest of that session stays a Terror.
🩹 Patch 3.2 / Season 14 (live 2026-05-22): every tier — including Fright — can drop Latent Sunder Charms, and the increased-Herald drop chance now starts at tier 1 (the "threshold" column above is pre-3.2 framing). Latent Sunders also now drop from any MF monster, and player-count no longer heavily modifies Latent / Worldstone Shard rates.
🩸 How to spawn it & climb the ladder
Hell-difficulty Terror Zones only — never Normal/Nightmare, never outside a TZ. Spawning runs on a hidden two-step token system:
• 1 · draw its ire (~2%) — every Champion, Unique, Superunique or Boss you kill inside the active Hell TZ has a ~2% chance to fire "You have drawn the ire of a Herald!" and bank an invisible token. Ire stacks up to 5× — chain elite kills fast and you can force several Heralds to spawn side-by-side.
• 2 · let it hunt you (~1%) — while you hold a token, every monster that spawns on a fresh, unexplored tile has a ~1% chance to turn into a Herald. Revealing new ground fires "A Herald is hunting you in [Zone]!".
• reveal, don't grind — once ire is drawn you don't need more kills; just walk into unvisited tiles so the engine has room to spawn one.
• every kill bumps the next Herald one tier higher — climb Fright → Dread → Fear → Horror → Terror (table below), and every tier carries an aura.
🛡️ Optimal farming strategies
A single 30–60 min TZ layout rarely has enough fresh tiles to chain all five tiers, so use one of these:
• Worldstone-Shard method — pop a Worldstone Shard to terrorize an entire act instead of one zone. That hands you a huge, continuous spread of fresh tiles — enough to draw ire and force Tier 4 → Tier 5 back-to-back without running out of map.
• zone-hopping overflow — if you draw ire just as a zone runs out of unexplored tiles, do not leave (leaving resets your tiers). Your ire token persists across the TZ rotation — wait for the next zone to go live, step in, and the Herald spawns on the first fresh tile you reveal.
Source: TheBugWarrior — "How to Farm Heralds & Sunder Charms (Terror Zones Guide)", Feb 2026.
🗺️ Where to draw ire — the best hunting grounds
The ~2% ire roll only fires off Champions / Uniques / Superuniques / Bosses, so you want the densest elite zones on the rotation — more elites per minute = more ire rolls per minute. Proven high-density picks (run whichever is the live Hell TZ, or terrorize its act with a Worldstone Shard):
• Chaos Sanctuary — the 3 Seal bosses + thick champion packs in one compact loop.
• Worldstone Keep → Throne of Destruction — dense floors plus Baal's 5 minions.
• The Pit (level 2) — very dense champion packs, short clear.
• Ancient Tunnels — compact, fast, single-screen clears (gold-chest bonus too).
Clear densely — don't skip packs — so the ire counter climbs fast, then start revealing fresh map.
Source: DiabloBytes — "Heralds of Terror" guide.
⚡ Work the two-step like a pro
Spawning is two independent rolls — draw ire (kills) then let it hunt you (reveal). Squeeze both:
• Bank ire first, then reveal. Every elite kill BOTH stacks an ire token (up to 5×) AND bumps the next Herald's tier — so grind a dense elite cluster first to stack tokens + climb the ladder, THEN push into virgin map so several high-tier Heralds can spawn at once.
• Reveal in big bites. The ~1% hunt roll fires per monster on fresh tiles — and one teleport into unexplored ground populates a whole room of monsters at once, each rolling independently. So uncover large chunks of new map fast; a single big teleport beats slow grinding over cleared ground.
• Elites only for ire — minions don't count. The ire list is Champion / Unique / Superunique / Boss; a unique's pack minions aren't on it, so don't burn time mopping up adds for the ire step.
• Watch for the lightning telegraph. A Herald spawn flashes a short lightning tell alongside the "A Herald is hunting you in [Zone]!" message — turn and engage it on sight.
• Never backtrack, never exit. Already-revealed tiles can't spawn a Herald, and exiting to the menu resets your whole tier climb back to Fright — stay in the session and always push into fresh ground.
• Speed > MF for volume. Post-3.2, Latent Sunders drop from any MF monster and player-count barely matters — so kill-speed and routing (more Heralds per hour) beat stacking Magic Find.
Sources: DiabloBytes — "Heralds of Terror" guide; derived from the spawn rules above.
💎 What it offers — the 6 Latent Sunder Charms
CharmBreaksBest forRenewed upgrade recipe
🔗 Latent → Renewed (Worldstone-Shard economy)
Two ways to get a Sunder: loot a Latent off a Herald, or cube 3 Worldstone Shards to roll a random Latent. Upgrade for extra random stats via cube: Latent Sunder + Perfect Gem + Rune + matching Worldstone Shard → Renewed. Region shard → immunity map:
• Northern (Act 5 — Crystalline/Halls/WSK/Throne) → Bone Break physical
• Western (Act 1 — Pit/Catacombs/Tristram) → Rotting Fissure poison
• Eastern (Act 2 — Far Oasis/Maggot Lair/Tombs) → Cold Rupture cold
• Southern (Act 3 — Spider Forest/Flayer/Travincal) → Crack of the Heavens lightning
• Deep (Act 4 — River of Flame/Chaos) → Flame Rift fire
• Black Cleft magic needs Southern + Deep + Northern.
Source: Maxroll.
⚔ Rules of thumb
Only ONE Sunder active at a time. The ~95% floor still leaves resist on the monster, so it cuts most of your damage — stack −enemy-resist, Conviction / Lower Resist, Amplify Damage and Crushing Blow to push below it. Match the Sunder to your build damage type (table above), farm that region's Heralds + shards, upgrade to Renewed once shards are spare.
🧪 Recipe / use
recipeLatent Sunder + Perfect Gem + Rune + matching Worldstone Shard → Renewed Sunder (per-charm combos in the table above) · or cube 3 Worldstone Shards → random Latent
⚠ importantOnly ONE Sunder active at a time · tiers reset to Fright if you exit to the main menu — stay in one game session to keep climbing.
⚠ Spawn figures (~2% ire / ~1% hunt) and tier behavior are the canonical community estimates (TheBugWarrior / DiabloBytes / Maxroll), not fabricated odds.

📸 How to take screenshots the AI can actually read — example below
The AI reads NAMES, not slots — items never need to be in a special position. What matters is that the name text is visible in the picture:
  • ✅ ground loot with Alt held — every name labeled, the best batch input
  • ✅ hover tooltip open over an item in stash/inventory
  • ✅ trade / vendor / mule windows where names show
  • ❌ a bare stash tab — that is item ART only, no names → little to read
Tip: after a session, stand over your pile, hold Alt, screenshot once — one picture logs the whole haul. The example image (click to enlarge) shows readable in-game text — this real stash screenshot (tooltip open on Spellsteel) is exactly what the AI read correctly in our live test.

Item Rarity & Colours

What every item colour means — how many mods it rolls, and how it ties into cubing & crafting

Normal · Socketed/Ethereal · Magic · Rare · Crafted · Set · Unique

▾
Every item in D2R is colour-coded by its rarity, and the colour tells you how many magic properties it can roll. This is the backbone of the cube: you craft onto a blue (magic) base, the cube hands you an orange (crafted) result, and you reroll yellow (rare) affixes — see the 🔨 Workshop & 🧊 Horadric recipes below.
Normal White0 mods
Base items with no magical properties — a blank slate.
🔩 The canvas for Runewords (socket the runes into a white base) and the start of most cube upgrades.
Socketed / Ethereal Greysockets · eth
Function like white items, but with open sockets (slot runes/gems/jewels) or Ethereal (can't be repaired, but higher base defence/damage).
🔩 Add sockets in the cube; Ethereal bases are prized for runewords & auto-repair builds.
Magic Blue1–2 mods
One prefix and/or one suffix. They can roll certain high-tier / max single stats (e.g. +3 to class skills on charms) that rares cannot.
🔨 The magic base you cube in crafting. Reroll a blue item with 3 Perfect gems (Horadric below).
Rare Yellow3–6 mods
Three to six random modifiers and a randomly-generated two-word name (not the "prefix + base + suffix" of magic items).
🎲 Renew its affixes by cubing 6 Perfect Skulls + the rare → a fresh roll (Horadric below).
Crafted Orange3 fixed + 1–4 random
Player-made in the Horadric Cube — a few guaranteed fixed mods plus 1–4 random ones.
🔨 This is exactly what the Crafted Items Workshop below builds (Caster / Blood / Safety / Hit Power).
Set Greenfixed + set bonus
Predetermined, themed items. Wearing several pieces of the same set unlocks extra hidden set bonuses.
📗 Track which pieces you own in the Item Set Tracker (Tools tab).
Unique Gold / Brownfixed
Fixed base stats, fixed unique properties, fixed name & its own graphic (e.g. The Stone of Jordan). Cannot be rerolled.
🏆 The grail items the Calculator ranks by drop odds. Cube to upgrade the tier (normal → exceptional → elite).
⚠ Colours follow the in-game name colour. Reign of the Warlock may add or retune affixes — verify in-game.

🏆 What you actually farm here
Rune volume + a broad unique/set pool
Not a single grail item — a density farm: ~400+ Hell Bovines per game for rune throughput plus a wide normal-monster unique/set pool. For the rune-specific detail, see the Cow Level card in the Runes tab.

Always-Hell-difficulty area accessed via cube. ~400 Hell Bovines + rare elite packs + the Cow King. Excellent for rune density (chipped/low-mid runes), set/unique drops, and general MF. Fast clears with AoE builds.

🦴 Step 1 — Get Wirt's Leg

Wirt's corpse is in Tristram (the original) — not the act 1 starting town. To reach Tristram:

  1. Rescue Cain in Act 1 (the Cairn Stones quest in Stony Field — activate them in order: 5 → 2 → 3 → 1 → 4)
  2. Red portal opens in Stony Field → Tristram
  3. Click Wirt's corpse → picks up Wirt's Leg
Note: You can grab Wirt's Leg on ANY difficulty as long as you rescue Cain on that difficulty. The Leg itself is the same item across all 3 difficulties — keep ONE in stash, it never breaks.

🌀 Step 2 — Cube the portal

Wirt's Leg + Tome of Town Portal (any)
→
red portal in Rogue Encampment · "Moo Moo Farm"
Cube must be in Rogue Encampment (Act 1 town). Recipe used in any other town does nothing. Town only — not in the field. Cube uses up both items.

⚠️ Step 3 — THE COW KING RULE

Critical: If you kill the Cow King on a difficulty, you can NEVER open the Cow Level on that difficulty again with that character. The recipe just fails silently.

Solo workaround: have an alt char open the portal for you. Online: someone else can open the portal in their game; you join.

Hardcore note: the Cow King has lightning enchant + amplify damage. Multi-shot kills him by accident easily — kite away or skip him entirely.

💎 Step 4 — What to farm

  • Runes: cows have a normal mob rune table — good for El/Eld/Tir/Nef/Ith/Tal/Ral/Ort up to ~Hel/Io. Not great for high runes (Countess + LK better) but ~400 cows = chipped runes flow steadily.
  • Sets/Uniques: Hell Bovines reach TC84 in Hell (TC87 in a Terror Zone) — see the full Hell Bovines drop card → for the verified per-difficulty pool. Can drop Hellbovine glove (cow-only specific drops), Trang's, Vidala's pieces.
  • Density: Hammerdin / Frozen Orb sorc / Lightning Fury ama / Mosaic sin — all clear 200+ cows/min. MF stacking is meaningful here.
For Konyo: Konyodin (Blessed Hammer + Concentration) is the king. Stack Goldwrap/Chance Guards/MF charms, run cows for an hour, walk away with 5-10 chipped runes + 1-2 set greens + general grail noise.

The only unique small charm in the game. Diablo Clone spawns on the realm-wide SoJ sell counter (public games only). One Anni per Clone kill: +1 all skills · +10-20 attributes · +10-20 all res · +5-10% experience. Click it for the full material card.

Server-wide world event. Über Diablo (DClone) walks the earth when enough Stones of Jordan are sold to vendors on a single server. Drops the only unique small charm in the game: the Annihilus (+1 all skills, +10-20 stats, +10-20 all res, +5-10% experience).

📡 Step 1 — Understand the spawn trigger

Each Battle.net server has its own SoJ counter. When 75-125 SoJs are sold to ANY NPC vendor on that server, the counter trips and Über Diablo spawns in EVERY Hell-difficulty game on that server. The 6 progression messages appear in the in-game chat as the counter climbs:

StageMessageSoJ count
1"Diablo has forsaken his most loyal servants..."~25%
2"Diablo's minions are growing in strength..."~50%
3"The Stone of Jordan summons Diablo..."~75%
4"Terror approaches Sanctuary..."~83%
5"Terror spreads across Sanctuary..."~92%
6"Diablo Walks the Earth" — DClone is up!100%

🎯 Step 2 — Catch the spawn window

Best practice: idle in the core of a high-count server when stage 4 or 5 appears. When stage 6 ("Diablo Walks the Earth") hits, DClone replaces the first super-unique monster you encounter in your Hell game (Bishibosh, Rakanishu, Pindleskin, Eldritch, Shenk, anyone). Spawn-camp a known super-unique location to fight him quickly.

SoJ trackers: sites like d2jsp / d2emu / dclone-tracker track public SoJ counters across servers. Refresh them to find a server about to pop. Multiple Annis can spawn in a single ladder reset cycle on busy servers.

Recommended counters:

Critical mistake: Don't fight him in a tight area (Pindleskin map, Stony Field corners). His skellie spawns + Charged Bolt nova lock you. Pull him to open ground (Outer Cloister, Bloody Foothills, Travincal main road).

🎄 22 Nights of Terror
Seasonal (Dec 13 – Jan 4) · daily-rotating modifiers · when Blizzard turns it on
nights
22

🏆 What this event gives
A seasonal farming window
Not a grail drop — a window. Dec 13 – Jan 4, daily-rotating terror-zone modifiers crank density + drop ceilings. The payoff is accelerated TZ farming (every grail reachable from a TZ becomes easier) while it is active.

Blizzard's holiday event. Active in all online modes (Classic excluded). The fabric of Sanctuary changes every 24 hours — a new gameplay modifier rotates daily for 22 days. Modifiers are visible via the in-game Message of the Day.

Typical modifiers (recurring across years):

  • 🎁 Holiday cheer — all monsters drop extra gold
  • ⚔️ Demonic frenzy — monster movement speed +50%
  • 💎 Greed — increased magic find for all players
  • 🔥 Hellfire — Hell-difficulty monsters spawn random super-uniques
  • 🌑 Endless terror — terror zones rotate every 15 min
  • 🩸 Bloodshed — all kills drop extra runes
  • 🎯 Champion of Sanctuary — boss kills grant a buff for the rest of the game
When it's on: usually runs Dec 13 → Jan 4 (D2R live servers, not RotW PTR). Free MF, free density, free XP. Sandwich an Anni hunt + a torch run into the modifier window.

⭐ The one rule that decides DPS
The one rule that decides DPS: a Fanaticism roll. Hephasto, the TZ Urdar and Lister can all carry it; bind, check the aura, save & exit and rebind until it's Fanaticism (Conviction → maps to Fanaticism in 3.2, so a "Conviction" roll is fine for fire builds).
🧮 Aura-level math — why TZ matters
Aura-level math (why TZ matters): bound-aura level = floor(min(monster mlvl, your level) ÷ 8). To hit the level-12 cap you need BOTH a mlvl-96 zone (a Terror Zone) AND your character at level 96+. Below that, the aura is weaker — so bind your damage targets in a TZ at high level.
⚠ Sourcing caveat
Caveat: only Lister, Hephasto and The Smith have fully-sourced fixed-Consume numbers; everything else is the family / tier behaviour, not a per-monster guarantee. Full sources live in the 📐 reference tab.

🔑 The hard-point gate — why most monsters say "Impossible" ▾

Bind Demon checks your hard points against the target's tier. Gear that adds +skills does NOT count toward this gate (it only helps the bound demon's aura level after the bind).

Monster tierName colorHard points neededAura Enchanted possible?
Regularwhite1 (any level)No
Championblue10No — champions give flat consume buff only
Unique packyellow15YES — this is the aura sweet spot
Super-Uniquegold/named20Fixed aura (The Smith, Lister, etc.)
The "Minion" tag: any demon labeled Minion in its tooltip is a summoned follower and CANNOT be bound regardless of your points. Find a standalone or pack-leader demon instead.
Bind chance (3.2, per Maxroll PTR notes): base chance scales with the target's missing HP. Death Mark synergy was halved (1% → 0.5% per level), the missing-HP benefit was reduced, and a max-HP cap that varies by each demon was introduced. Lower the target's HP as far as you can before casting — patch notes don't publish a fixed % threshold.

🔁 Why "the aura changes" — reroll to Fanaticism
Why "the aura changes": the Aura Enchanted aura is random per spawn (maxroll: "the boss spawns with a random Paladin Aura that scales based on the mLVL"). That's exactly why you save & exit and rebind until Fanaticism — and why a mlvl-96 Terror Zone matters: it's the only place Fanaticism reaches its level-12 cap. The level is ALSO capped by your own character level at bind time, so bind at lvl 96+.
🩺 What the health-bar actually shows
What the monster's health-bar actually shows (in-game): a Hell unique rolls 3 random modifiers — but a super-unique (Lister / Hephasto) also has its own fixed mods + its immunities, and the health-bar stacks all of them together. That's why you'll often count 8–9 lines on one boss (e.g. Aura Enchanted · Extra Strong · Extra Fast · Cursed · Immune to Physical · Immune to Fire …). Only the random rolls + the aura are rerollable — the immunities come from the monster's own base resistances. Lister specifically: fixed Spectral Hit + 2 random rolls in Hell (1 in NM) — so Aura Enchanted and Stone Skin are each a random roll, and a spawn carrying BOTH used both Hell slots.
👁️ Can you see the aura before binding? — yes, by its effects
The nameplate never names the aura — the modifier line only ever says “Aura Enchanted”. But the aura is already active while Lister lives, so you identify it before binding: his minions show the aura animation under their feet (diablo2.io mod Schnorki — only the aura-bearer shows the text, the whole pack shows the graphic) · Conviction = your resists/defense visibly drop · Holy Freeze = you’re permanently chilled · Fanaticism = the pack attacks noticeably faster. Post-3.2 corollary: a removed aura you SEE live remaps 1:1 at bind — spotting Conviction on a live Lister = a guaranteed Fanaticism pet.
📸 What you see is what you bind — plus your own buffs on top: the bind snapshots every displayed affix (diablo2.io skill page: the demon “keeps all the affixes it had before being bound” and persists through games) — Stone Skin, Extra Strong, Cursed, the immunities: all kept exactly as shown. The one exception is the aura, remapped per the 3.2 table below. On top of the snapshot your skills ADD affixes at bind time: Bind Demon lvl 5 → Extra Strong · 10 → Extra Fast · 15 → Spectral Hit · 20 → Aura Enchanted (community-sourced — diablo2.io + aoeah agree; no official table), plus Bind Demon’s own damage bonus and Demonic Mastery’s passive damage/AR/attack-speed. Since a super-unique needs Bind Demon 20 anyway, EVERY Lister you bind is granted Aura Enchanted even if he didn’t spawn with it — so hunt the Stone Skin spawn for the phys-immune body; the aura arrives with the bind regardless, then save & exit and rebind until it’s Fanaticism.
🧮 The 8-ability math — don’t hunt rolls the skill gives you FREE: a super-unique bind needs Bind Demon 20, so ALL FOUR skill grants are always on your pet: Extra Strong (5) · Extra Fast (10) · Spectral Hit (15) · Aura Enchanted (20). A spawn roll that duplicates a grant adds NOTHING. The fixed bars already burn some: Hephasto = Aura Enchanted + Spectral Hit fixed (2 of the 4, PureDiablo-verified) · Lister = Spectral Hit fixed (1 of 4) · The Smith = Extra Fast fixed (1 of 4). So the rolls worth hunting are the ones OUTSIDE the grant list: Stone Skin (the Hell-Lister immunity-maker) · Magic Resistant · Cursed (post-3.2 only a 5% amp proc). A Stone Skin + Cursed (or Magic Resistant) Lister ends at ~8 distinct lines: fixed Spectral + granted ES/EF/AE + 2 real rolls + Immune to Physical + Immune to Fire — the max-ability pet. The one nuance: an Aura Enchanted ROLL is slot-redundant but buys visibility (read Conviction live → guaranteed Fanaticism); the granted aura is a blind ~1-in-5. Max abilities vs guaranteed aura — your pick per spawn.
🧬 The Hell elite-affix pool
A Hell unique rolls 3 random modifiers; a super-unique stacks its fixed mods + immunities on top — only the random rolls + the aura are rerollable.
Aura Enchanted
Boss carries a random Paladin aura (scales by mlvl, tiles above) — random per spawn, and the nameplate never names it: read it from the pack’s aura animation + your own debuffs · ⭐ THE target — reroll to Fanaticism
Extra Strong
Bonus damage + attack rating · ⚠ BD grant at skill 5 — on a 20-pt bind a ROLLED copy is a wasted slot
Extra Fast
+100% Faster Run/Walk for boss + minions · ⚠ BD grant at skill 10 — rolled copy = wasted slot
Cursed
75% chance to apply Amplify Damage on hit · ⚠️ 3.2 nerf: once BOUND the proc drops to 5% — still hurts you while you fight him, but the old self-amp triple-damage trick is gone
Stone Skin
+50% Physical Damage Resist + doubled base defense · ✅ on Hell Lister AND Hell Hephasto it’s the immunity-maker: both have 50 base phys (PureDiablo), +50 = 100% → the pet IS Immune to Physical (NM either: 0 base — stays a mere 50%; Hephasto’s slot-1 screenshot proves it in-game. The Smith is the exception: 25 base Hell → Stone Skin = 75%, tanky but NOT immune)
Spectral Hit
Adds random elemental damage to attacks · ⚠ BD grant at skill 15 — and fixed on Lister AND Hephasto anyway
Multiple Shots
Fires 3 missiles per attack (ranged types only) · ✅ ranged pets only
Magic Resistant
Adds elemental resistances · ✅ NOT a grant — a real roll: pure pet survivability on a max-ability hunt
Cold / Fire / Lightning Enchanted
Adds that element + a death-detonation / charged bolts · neutral on a pet
Mana Burn
Drains mana on hit, converts it to the boss's life · ⚠️ this is Lister's "I can't" while you fight him — irrelevant once bound
Teleportation
Boss teleports and heals up to 30% max life · ⚠️ annoying to kill; fine once bound
Immune to Physical
Total physical resist ≥ 100% — base stat or base 50 + a Stone Skin roll (Hell Lister) · ✅ on a bound pet = near-unkillable vs physical attackers
Immune to Cold
Base cold resist ≥ 100% · ✅ your pet can't be frozen or chilled — a big survival win
Immune to Fire / Lightning / Poison
That element's base resist ≥ 100% · ✅ pet shrugs off that element (e.g. survives the Uber elemental rooms)
📐 The ÷8 myth, busted
The ÷8 myth, busted: the per-aura divisors above mean only Fanaticism / Conviction / Holy Shock use ÷8 — Holy Freeze is ÷7, Holy Fire ÷6, Blessed Aim ÷5. Full sources in the 📐 reference tab.

🔁 Removed-aura remap — deterministic 1:1 (3.2 LIVE)
Removed-aura remap (3.2 LIVE notes — deterministic 1:1): when a bound demon's Aura Enchanted would roll a removed aura, it maps to exactly one replacement — Conviction→Fanaticism · Might→Concentration · Holy Fire→Vigor · Holy Shock→Vigor · Blessed Aim→Thorns · Holy Freeze→Holy Freeze (unchanged). So the 5 possible results are Fanaticism / Concentration / Vigor / Thorns / Holy Freeze — reroll until Fanaticism. Hard-coded super-unique auras (Smith's Holy Fire, Lister's Meditation) pre-exist the bind and are NOT remapped. The PTR notes worded this loosely as "one of four"; the live Season 14 notes published the explicit 1:1 table above. Pre-3.2 demons you'd bound with a removed aura were remapped on patch day.
⚠ Divisors, the level-12 Fanaticism cap and the affix pool are verified mechanics (Maxroll / diablo2.io — full sources in the 📐 reference tab), not fabricated values.

📍 How the tiers actually work (read first) ▾

Champions and Uniques are NOT different monsters. They are the blue (champion) and yellow (unique pack) spawns of the same demon families. A Pit Lord can spawn white (1 pt), champion (10 pts), or unique (15 pts). Only Super-Uniques are specific named bosses.

So the tables below list the demon families and where they spawn densely. You hunt the area, then bind whichever blue/yellow version you find. Difficulty: Hell for everything — it gives the highest monster level, which means the strongest consume bonus and aura. A Hell Terror Zone is even better (lvl 96+ = max aura) once you are level 94+.

Demon-type only: Bind Demon ignores Undead (skeletons, Doom Knights, zombies) and Humans (Council, Barbarians). Hover the monster — the tooltip must say Demon and must NOT say Minion.
💡 Snapshot rule — gear up BEFORE you bind: a bound demon's stats and affixes are locked at the instant of binding (diablo2.io: a bound demon's characteristics are "snapshotted at the time of binding"). Equipping +skills gear or spending more hard points afterward does nothing to a demon you've already bound. So stack every +Bind Demon / +Warlock skills item you own, land the bind, then swap back to your normal gear — the demon keeps the stronger snapshot.
⚠️ Channel it — don't let go, don't hotkey it: Patch 3.2 moved the bind roll to frame 24 with no minimum-duration floor, so releasing the button before ~1 second means it never binds. Hold the cast until the demon is actually bound. And never put Bind Demon on a hotkey — an accidental bind instantly kills your current demon, aura and all (diablo2.io).

The two messages mean different things: "Impossible" = this target type/tier can never be bound by you right now (wrong type, Minion, or not enough points). "I can't" = you're out of mana or the cast was interrupted (Lister's Mana Burn does this — refill and retry).
Common traps you already hit: Travincal Council = Human (no). Defiled Warriors around Lister = Undead (no). The "Minion"-tagged Pit Lord in River of Flame = summoned follower (no — find a non-Minion one). Lister himself = Super-Unique, needs 20 points.
The 5-second check: hover → must say Demon, must NOT say Minion, must be a tier your points cover, must be low HP. All four true = it binds.

⚡ The Terror Zone shortcut (level 94+) ▾

Once you hit level 94, every demon in a Hell Terror Zone is level 96+, which produces the maximum aura level on bind. A lvl 12 Fanaticism from a TZ demon matches what a high-level Paladin provides.

  1. Reach lvl 94 (you are at 90 — ~4 levels of TZ/Baal farming)
  2. Enter any Hell Terror Zone with a demon population
  3. Find an Aura Enchanted unique demon (15 hard points), weaken it, bind
  4. If the aura is not Fanaticism, release and rebind the next one — no need to hunt specific named bosses
This removes the tedious super-unique hunt entirely. TZ + 15 hard points + lvl 94 = best practical bind in the game for an Echo Warlock.

🔱 For Konyo — Echoing Strike verdict ▾

Your build deals weapon-based magic damage and scales through Eldritch synergies, not pets. Here is the honest cost-benefit at lvl 90:

10 hard pts
Champion · flat buff, NO aura
15 hard pts
Unique · Fanaticism possible ⭐
20 hard pts
Super-unique · Hephasto reroll ⭐

If you want a real damage bind: go 15 hard points, farm River of Flame yellow packs for an Aura Enchanted Fanaticism roll. Fanaticism boosts your Echo hits AND your merc. That is the cheapest tier that earns its skill points on this build.

If you can afford 20 hard points: Hephasto the Armorer (River of Flame, Hellforge) is the cleanest endgame bind — he spawns solo, is always Aura Enchanted with a random aura, and sits at mlvl 88 (aura 11). Just save+exit/rejoin and rebind until you roll Fanaticism. No pack to clear, right next to the Hellforge WP. For aura 12, rebind him (or any demon) in a Hell Terror Zone at mlvl 96 with your Warlock at lvl 96+.
Opportunity cost: 15 hard points + ~5 prereqs = 20 points pulled out of Echoing Strike / Mirrored Blades / Blade Warp synergies. At lvl 90 with ~101 points, you can afford ONE maxed synergy fewer to fund it. At lvl 99 you can have both. If you can grind to 95+, do that before committing.
Cheapest splash (1 point): if you just want a tanky pet, 1 hard point binds any regular (white, non-Minion) demon — Urdar or Pit Lord in River of Flame. No aura, but it soaks hits and pulls aggro. Costs almost nothing.
Don't spend points on Demonic Mastery: it raises your Summon-demon count (Goatman / Tainted / Defiler), not your bind count — and your bound demon is hard-capped at 1 regardless of mastery rank. With no summon skills on an Echoing Strike build, Demonic Mastery does nothing for you. Those points belong in Echoing Strike / Mirrored Blades / Blade Warp.

🛡️ Top 3 dream immunity rolls ▾

Your bound demon is a pet, so the immunities on its health-bar are pure survivability. They can't be rerolled — they come from the monster's own base resists — so it's really a question of which super-unique you bind. The tankiest binds stack Physical Immunity plus one element. Here are the three health-bar immunity profiles worth hunting, best→worst for a pet that simply won't die.

★ Top 3 immunity profiles to bind ★
1 🔥 Immune to Physical + Immune to FireProven — Lister the Tormentor. Tanks every melee & missile hit plus all fire packs; the community-OP bind. The only profile confirmed in-game (his health-bar is shown in his ID card). S
2 ❄️ Immune to Physical + Immune to ColdThe cold analogue: a cold-immune pet can't be frozen or chilled, so it never loses attack speed in cold-heavy zones (Frigid Highlands, Nihlathak, Frozen packs). Same melee-tank value as #1. A
3 ⚡ Immune to Physical + Immune to LightningThe rarer roll — lightning is the hardest-hitting ranged element (Gloams, Tesla packs), so a phys+lightning pet shrugs off the deadliest spike damage in the game. Hunt it for lightning-heavy Terror Zones. A
Why Physical first: physical is the most common damage type in the game, so a Physical-Immune pet tanks nearly everything that isn't elemental — pair it with the element your farm zone throws hardest. Note: only the Physical+Fire profile (Lister) is screenshot-verified; the cold & lightning profiles are the survival targets to look for, not a claim about a specific named monster.

🎯 Best roll — what to look for ▾

After the 3.2 remap a bound demon's Aura Enchanted lands on one of five results. Here they are ranked best→worst for an Echoing Strike Warlock — tap any row to open its aura ID card.

Bottom line: only Fanaticism is worth keeping — save & exit and rebind until you see it. Everything else is a reroll.

The aura is only one line. On its in-game health-bar a bound super-unique stacks its fixed mods + its 3 random Hell rolls + its immunities — often 8–9 attributes in total, so a perfect roll is rare. Beyond a Fanaticism aura, these are the 3 damage affixes worth rerolling for on an Echoing Strike pet build — effects per the Arreat Summit bonus tables.

★ Top 3 bind affix buffs to look for ★
1 💪 Extra Strong×2.5 physical damage on your bound demon — the single biggest pet-DPS multiplier in the pool. Stacks multiplicatively with your demon's own boosts. S
2 🩸 CursedIts hits cast Amplify Damage on the enemy — −100% physical resist and it strips Physical Immunity, multiplying both your demon's hits and your own. A
3 ⚡ Extra Fast+25% attack speed and faster movement — more hits per second, and the demon keeps pace with you between packs instead of lagging behind. A
▾ See the full bind-affix pool — all 12 ranked (tap to expand)
★ Every super-unique boss modifier, ranked for a bind ★
1 💪 Extra Strong×2.5 physical damage — the single biggest pet-DPS multiplier in the pool, stacking multiplicatively with your demon's own boosts. The roll you reroll for. S
2 🩸 CursedIts hits cast Amplify Damage — −100% enemy physical resist and it strips Physical Immunity, multiplying both your demon's hits and your own. A
3 ⚡ Extra Fast+25% attack speed and faster movement — more hits per second, and the demon keeps pace with you between packs instead of lagging behind. A
4 ✨ Aura EnchantedThe rerollable aura line itself — lands on Fanaticism / Holy Freeze / Concentration / Vigor / Thorns. Fanaticism is the jackpot (see the ranked aura table above). A
5 ❄️ Cold EnchantedBonus cold damage on the demon's hits, and its cold chills & slows whatever it touches — a little extra damage plus genuine crowd-control utility. B
6 🌈 Spectral HitEach swing adds a random element of bonus damage — free extra damage on top of the demon's physical, and it helps chip immunes. B
7 🔥 Fire EnchantedBonus fire damage on hits + a fire burst when the demon scores a kill, plus a touch of extra resist. Modest, but never a wasted roll. B
8 ⚡ Lightning EnchantedReleases Charged Bolts when the demon is struck and on a kill — a small spray of extra lightning. Minor, but harmless padding damage. B
9 🪨 Stone SkinGreatly increased defense + 50% physical-damage resist — no offense, but a noticeably tankier pet. On Hell Lister (50 base phys) it stacks to 100% = Immune to Physical, turning this C-roll into a top survival pick there. C
10 🛡️ Magic ResistantBoosted elemental resistances on the demon — pure survivability against caster packs. Fine, but it does nothing for your damage. C
11 🎯 Multiple ShotsFires a spread of missiles — only does anything on a ranged attacker, so on a melee bound demon it's effectively a dead roll. Reroll. D
12 🌀 Mana Burn · TeleportationMana Burn drains enemy mana (worthless for a pet) and Teleportation makes the demon blink around erratically, losing your packs. Both are reroll-now. D
Effects per the Arreat Summit boss-modifier tables — a bound super-unique keeps whatever modifiers it spawned with and turns them on your enemies. The top 3 are the only damage keepers; everything B-and-below is a bonus-at-best, D is an outright reroll. BD-20 lens: this podium ranks raw affix power — but Extra Strong / Extra Fast / Spectral Hit come FREE from Bind Demon 5/10/15, so for ROLL-hunting value see the 🧮 8-ability math above: the rolls that add anything are Stone Skin / Magic Resistant / Cursed.
Honorable mentions: Stone Skin (tankier pet — and on Hell Lister it stacks his 50 base phys to 100% = Immune to Physical) and Spectral Hit (free random elemental on every swing) are fine bonus rolls. Avoid: Mana Burn and Teleportation do nothing useful for a bound pet.
Best survival rolls: because your bound demon is a pet, its immunities are pure survivability — an Immune-to-Physical demon is near-unkillable and Immune-to-Cold can't be frozen. The dream bind: Fanaticism aura + a Physical or Cold immunity + a non-grant roll (Stone Skin / Magic Resistant — Extra Strong comes free from Bind Demon 5) = a hard-hitting pet that simply won't die.

🎯The two drop filtersEvery drop passes a TC check + a qlvl check — both must pass or it can never drop▾

2. qlvl check: monster mlvl ≥ item qlvl

🗡️Warlock skill kitWhat Echoing Strike actually does — the active skills behind the bind build▾

The 🔱 binds tab assumes you already run the meta build — here is the kit it is built around. Echoing Strike is the attack; a wall of summoned demons (Demonic Mastery) tanks and feeds Consume buffs; and a bound demon carries your aura. This is the verified Reign-of-the-Warlock Season-14 skill list.
SkillRoleWhat it does (verified)
Echoing StrikeMain attackUses your Faster Cast Rate to spawn up to 5 echoes of your weapon that fly out in a cone and return after hitting terrain or reaching the arc's end. Cursor distance sets the fan — hold closer to spread it wide, farther to narrow it. Scales with weapon base damage + Enhanced Damage + off-weapon ED.
Mirrored BladesSynergy (max)Swings multiple times at a single target — the single-target / boss-damage synergy.
Blade WarpSynergy + mobilityAn Echoing Strike synergy that doubles as your primary teleport-style mobility until you get Enigma.
Hex BaneSynergy (max)Adds Magic damage and reduces enemy Defense to help you land hits.
Levitation MasteryPassiveIncreases damage, attack rating and critical-strike chance, and lowers your weapon requirements.
Demonic MasterySummonsBuffs and caps your summoned demons — 10 points → 2 Summon Defilers to spread damage and soak aggro. The hard-point summon cap and the Goatman / Tainted / Defiler field detail are on the 🔱 binds tab.
ConsumeBuff engineSacrifice a summoned demon for a buff — a Summon Defiler consume raises your Magic damage and cuts enemy Magic resistance; a Goatman consume gives +% damage. Full per-demon consume detail on the binds tab.
Bind DemonAura carrierGrab a demon — ideally one rolling Curse + Fanaticism — for a massive damage boost. Full bind mechanics → binds tab.
Speed target: maintain the 125% Faster Cast Rate breakpoint — Echoing Strike fires off your FCR, so it is a top gearing priority. FCR / FHR caster tables are in the 📐 Breakpoints section below.
How the kit loops: summon a wall of demons → they tank and let you Consume for damage / resist-shred → Bind one for a permanent Fanaticism aura → spam Echoing Strike at 125% FCR while Mirrored Blades and Hex Bane carry single-target. That is the whole engine the binds tab optimizes.

Source: maxroll.gg · Echoing Strike Warlock guide (Season 14, Reign of the Warlock) + icy-veins Echoing Strike skill page. Skill behaviour is RotW-current as of Season 14; exact synergy percentages and point breakpoints can be retuned per season — verify the live tooltips in-game. Bind / aura / Consume deep mechanics live on the 🔱 binds tab.

📐MF mathThe diminishing-returns formula behind your effective magic find▾

Effective MF = (Gear MF × 100) / (Gear MF + Factor)
Unique factor = 250 · Set = 500 · Rare = 600
100% MF
28.6%
effective unique
300% (ref)
54.5%
effective unique
699% (you)
73.7%
effective unique
1500% (max)
85.7%
effective unique
What Magic Find does NOT touch: MF only improves the quality roll (magic → rare → set → unique) on items that can roll those qualities — and per the curve above it is most effective for uniques (factor 250) and weakest for rares (factor 600). It does nothing for runes, gems, jewels, charms, gold, quest / guaranteed drops, gambling or crafting, and it never changes which item type drops. An Ist rune or a Sunder charm is found at the same rate at 0% MF as at 700%.
Gold Find is a separate stat (not MF): it only enlarges the gold piles monsters drop — handy for funding gambling, repairs and cube-rerolls — but it has zero effect on item drops or their quality. Stack it on a dedicated gold run, not on a grail run.

👥What the P# slider actually doesMore quantity via shrinking NoDrop — never better quality (that's MF's job)▾

/players N shrinks each monster's NoDrop, so it drops MORE items (quantity) — it never changes drop QUALITY (that's MF's job). How much depends on the monster's base NoDrop q:
multiplier = (1 − qᵏ) / (1 − q),  k = 1 + floor(N / 2)
Breakpoints, not a smooth ramp: /p1 (solo) is the ×1.00 baseline; drops step up at /p2, /p4, /p6, /p8, with /p2=/p3, /p4=/p5, /p6=/p7 as identical pairs. Higher player count = slower kills, so it's a quantity-vs-speed trade, never a quality gain.
It moves 3 of the 4 boss tiers — only the guaranteed droppers (q=0) ignore it entirely. Multipliers shown at /players 8 (Hell):
tierbossesNoDrop q×@ /p8
🐝 High-density packsPit · Cows0.625×2.41
💰 Heavy droppersAndariel · Nihlathak · Travincal0.28–0.35×1.39–1.52
👹 The Prime EvilsMephisto · Diablo · Baal0.183×1.22
🔓 Guaranteed droppersCountess · Duriel · Pindleskin0.0×1.00 · P#-PROOF

Guaranteed droppers — they always spill their full table, so extra players add only HP, never loot (these carry the · P#-PROOF tag on their cards).

🛡️Mercenary mechanicsHireling auras, hire-difficulty rules & best merc gear (vanilla D2R)▾

A Warlock buffs his merc — and an Act 2 merc's aura buffs you back. So the merc is a real part of the build, not just a body. Mechanics below are maxroll-sourced vanilla D2R; the drop-rate numbers everywhere else on this site stay silospen-RoW.
RotW caveat: aura names, availability and merc scaling are vanilla D2R (maxroll). Reign of the Warlock may rebalance them — verify the aura you actually get in-game; your firsthand RotW experience overrides any cell here.
The four hirelings — one active at a time:
ActHirelingHired fromFights with
Act 1Rogue ScoutKashyaBow — Cold or Fire arrow variant
Act 2Desert Mercenary ⭐GreizSpear / polearm + a permanent party aura — the one almost everyone runs
Act 3IronwolfAshearaSword + shield, casts Cold / Fire / Lightning spells
Act 5BarbarianQual-KehkOne- or two-handed melee, Stun / Bash
Act 2 Desert Mercenary auras — pick by the difficulty you HIRE in:
Greiz menuNormal & HellNightmare
CombatPrayer (heal pulse)Thorns (reflect)
DefensiveDefiance (+defense)Holy Freeze ⭐ (chills + slows everything)
OffensiveBlessed Aim (+AR)Might ⭐ (+% phys damage)
The one rule: hire your Act 2 merc in NIGHTMARE. Hell mercs revert to the Normal auras, so the meta picks — Holy Freeze (Defensive · the survival king, slows the whole screen) and Might (Offensive · raw party damage) — only exist on the Nightmare menu. Hire there, then level him to Hell.
Revive cost & scaling:
revive gold = min( int(hlvl × hlvl / 2) × 15 , 50,000 ) — capped at 50k gold (a lvl-92+ merc hits the cap). The merc levels with you and inherits life/AR/damage from its level; an Act 2 merc deals a % of its equipped weapon's damage, so its gear matters more than its base.
Best Act 2 merc gear (3 slots — weapon · helm · armor):
SlotTop picksWhy
WeaponInfinity · Insight · Reaper's Toll · Pride · ObedienceInfinity = Conviction aura (−enemy res, breaks Lightning immunes) · Insight = Meditation mana engine · Reaper's Toll = Decrepify on hit · Pride = Concentration · Obedience = budget Crushing Blow
HelmAndariel's Visage · Tal Rasha's Horadric Crest · Vampire Gaze · Crown of ThievesAndariel's (socket a Ruby / rainbow to patch its −30 fire res) = +2 skills, 20 IAS, big life leech — the BiS merc helm
ArmorFortitude · Treachery · Stone · DuressFortitude = +300% ED + 25 all res + Chilling Armor (BiS) · Treachery = budget Fade (25 res / DR) + 45 IAS + Venom
Use ETHEREAL bases on a merc: mercs ignore durability, so an ethereal weapon/armor never breaks and you keep the +50% ethereal damage/defense for free. The single biggest cheap upgrade.
For Konyo (Warlock): your Lister bind already gives you a permanent Lvl-15 Meditation, so an Insight merc is redundant — run Infinity instead (its Conviction shreds resists for your elemental Echo and breaks Lightning immunes), or a Holy Freeze merc if you want the screen-wide slow for safety. See the 🔱 binds tab for the Meditation source.

Source: maxroll.gg · Mercenary Mechanics resource (vanilla D2R mechanics). Aura specifics to be confirmed against Reign of the Warlock in-game.

🎲GamblingBuy unidentified items for gold — a flat shot at rares, sets & uniques (no MF needed)▾

Gambling = buying a normal-looking unidentified magic item from a town vendor; the game re-rolls its quality the instant you buy it. It's the one drop source Magic Find does NOT touch — only your character level matters (it sets the item level). Gold-rich and grail-hunting? This is a flat, repeatable shot at slot-specific uniques like the Stone of Jordan.
Who gambles — every act, every difficulty:
ActGambling NPC
Act 1Gheed
Act 2Elzix
Act 3Alkor
Act 4Jamella
Act 5Anya (also Nihlathak)

The act, difficulty and NPC you pick have zero effect on the odds — they're identical everywhere. Pick whichever town you're already in.

The fixed quality odds — per item bought (these never change):
QualityChanceExact ratio
Magic89.85%1797 / 2000
Rare10%200 / 2000
Set0.10%2 / 2000
Unique0.05%1 / 2000
The mechanics that decide WHAT you can roll:
  • Item level = your character level (with a small ±variance). A higher clvl unlocks higher-tier uniques in the gamble pool — gamble on your highest character.
  • Past character level 56, every item type can appear in the gambling window; below that the slot pool is restricted and widens gradually.
  • Rings & amulets are ALWAYS in the window — one of each, at a fixed gold cost (≈50,000 ring / ≈63,000 amulet, level-independent). Other slots scale in price with your level. That fixed cost makes rings/amulets the reliable reset-and-rebuy targets.
  • Magic Find does nothing here. Gold Find only helps you afford more rolls — it never improves the odds above.
What's worth gambling for (vanilla high-value targets — confirm the exact unique exists in Reign of the Warlock):
SlotWhy gamble itDream uniques
RingsFixed cheap cost, always in window — the classic SoJ huntStone of Jordan · Bul-Kathos' Wedding Band · Nature's Peace · Raven Frost · Dwarf Star
AmuletsFixed cost, always in window; rolls +skill rares tooMara's Kaleidoscope · The Eye of Etlich · Highlord's Wrath · Seraph's Hymn
Circlets / CoronetsCan roll +class-skill magic/rare bases — a cheap skiller helm+2 class-skill circlet · rare 2-skill coronet
Read the odds honestly: the 1 / 2000 is the chance the bought item is some unique of that slot — which unique then depends on that slot's treasure class at your item level. So a specific Stone of Jordan is rarer than 1/2000. Gamble for the slot, reset the window between buys, and only do it with overflowing gold (a roll is individually cheap, but you'll buy thousands).
For Konyo (Warlock): ring/amulet gambling is the only MF-independent path to a Stone of Jordan or Mara's. Bank gold from Travincal council runs, then sit on the highest-level character and reset-buy rings between farming sessions — every SoJ you gamble is also another DClone trigger you control.

Source: maxroll.gg Gambling resource + fextralife D2R gamble-odds (1797 / 200 / 2 / 1 per 2000). Core gamble mechanics are base-game D2R; Reign of the Warlock may add or retune the unique pool — confirm which ring/amulet uniques are actually gambleable in-game.

Roll quality — craft on a Hell base, at high clvl:
crafted ilvl = int(0.5 × clvl) + int(0.5 × base ilvl) (cap 99). A high-ilvl base crafted by a high-level character unlocks the most random affixes — an ilvl 71+ result can roll the full 4 extra affixes on top of the 3 guaranteed. The jewel can be magic or rare; the rune is the cheapest of the recipe. Reroll the same recipe until the random affixes land where you want them.
For Konyo (Warlock): Caster is your craft — a crafted amulet or ring (Perfect Amethyst) guarantees FCR + mana, the cheapest way to push Echoing Strike toward its cast breakpoints while you hunt the unique upgrades. Pair this with the ⚡ Breakpoints section below to know exactly how much FCR you still need.

Source: maxroll.gg · Crafted Items (vanilla D2R mechanics — recipes/mods are base-game; Reign of the Warlock may retune affix pools, verify in-game).

⚡BreakpointsFaster Cast Rate & Faster Hit Recovery frame thresholds▾

D2R runs animations at 25 frames/sec, and an animation always takes a whole number of frames. Faster Cast Rate (FCR) and Faster Hit Recovery (FHR) cut a frame off only at fixed breakpoint thresholds — every % between two breakpoints is wasted until you reach the next one. So you don't stack FCR endlessly; you stack to the next breakpoint and stop.
RotW caveat — IMPORTANT: the tables below are the canonical vanilla Sorceress (caster) breakpoints — the right reference for a cast build. Reign of the Warlock's base animation may differ. Treat these as a starting reference: count your own cast/recovery frames in-game (or confirm the Warlock's base class) before committing gear. Your firsthand RotW timing overrides any cell here.

The other two, briefly: Faster Run/Walk (FRW) has breakpoints too but the gains are small — most players just take what their boots/gear give. IAS / weapon speed matters for melee attack speed and is highly weapon-dependent (it's not a flat table) — largely irrelevant to a cast build. Faster Block Rate (FBR) only applies if you wear a shield and actively hold block; a caster usually skips it.
For Konyo (Warlock): the Sorceress table above is a reference, not your exact table — the Warlock has his own cast-rate breakpoints (note the Sorc table jumps 105 → 200 with no row between, so it can’t show a 125 point). maxroll’s Echoing Strike guide publishes 125% FCR as the build’s priority breakpoint (the exact frame count isn’t published — confirm in-game). The cheapest way there: a Caster-crafted amulet / ring (🔨 section above, Perfect Amethyst guarantees FCR) plus FCR uniques (Magefist gloves, an FCR ring, a +FCR caster ammy). Hit 125% FCR, then stop stacking FCR and pour the rest into mana / resists. See the ⚔️ Warlock skill kit section (Reference tab) for the full Echoing Strike loop.

📜Tristram StonesThe Cain rescue rerun — cube 4 stones per act for a +1 socket weapon▾

After Cain is rescued in each act, you can cube 4 stones from Act bosses for a +1 socket weapon at Larzuk per act. Each Cain visit = 1 cube. Most ignore this past Act 1.

🎯Confidence formulaHow many runs for a given drop confidence — 50% ≈ 0.69×X, 95% ≈ 3×X▾

runs = log(1 - confidence) / log(1 - 1/dropChance)

Practical: chance 1:X → 50% conf ≈ 0.693 × X, 95% ≈ 3 × X, 99% ≈ 4.6 × X.

🎲 What the drop simulator actually shows

D2R drops are pure RNG. "1:836 Shako" means each kill rolls a fresh 1-in-836 chance — not "guaranteed in 912 runs". You might get one in 100 kills, or do 3000 and get zero.

The sim runs your scenario 20 times so you see the actual variance — that ~58% of 500-kill Meph sessions get zero Shakos at the verified rate, even though 0.55 is the math-expected number. Calibrates expectations against tilt.

Everything saves to localStorage: MF, wishlist, owned, statues, sort orders, boss filters. Reset button in footer.

📖 D2R Drop Mechanics — what TC and qlvl mean

TC = Treasure Class

Every unique/set item has a TC number that defines which drop pool it lives in. A monster can only drop items whose TC is ≤ the monster's effective TC.

Example: Tyrael's Might is TC87. Hell Mephisto caps at TC78 → he can NEVER drop Tyrael's, no matter your MF. Hell Diablo is TC87 → he can.

qlvl = Quality Level

Each item has a qlvl (its required item level). The boss's monster level (mlvl) must be ≥ the item's qlvl for it to drop.

Example: Mara's Kaleidoscope qlvl 67. Normal Andariel mlvl 12 → blocked. Hell Andariel mlvl 75 → fine.

Reading the cells in this app

⬜ 1:X → estimated chance · TC-ratio model · live MF-adjusted

🔒 green border → verified anchor against silospen / pairofdocs (3 anchors in this build)

⭐ green cell → best difficulty for this item on this boss

⛔ orange → qlvl block · boss mlvl too low · go to higher difficulty

⛔ pink → TC block · this boss CAPS below this item's TC · UNFIXABLE on this boss

Tier badges

uber → only drops from special encounters (Annihilus, Hellfire Torch, Tyrael's)

grail → traditional Holy Grail items (need-to-have)

high → top builds use these (Mara's, Shako, Arach, etc)

common → mid/low tier — useful sometimes

set → set piece

special → keys, runes, charms not bound to TC

About chances

The number after 1: is the EXPECTED runs for ONE drop on average. 1:836 = 836 runs avg. At 50% confidence you'll typically need ~580 runs; at 95% you'll typically need ~2,500.
